panels.title: Order flow — is the desk actually trading?
Orders submitted (5m rate)
panels.description: The first question a trading dashboard must answer: is anything happening at all? The engine panels can look perfectly healthy while the desk has not sent an order in an hour.

panels.title: Fill ratio (5m)
panels.description: Orders reaching 'filled' as a share of all terminal outcomes. A falling ratio with steady submissions means the venue is rejecting or the book has moved away — two different problems that look identical on an order-count panel alone.

panels.title: Terminal outcomes by status
panels.description: filled / cancelled / rejected split. A rise in cancelled is an execution problem; a rise in rejected is a control or data problem. Aggregating them hides which.

panels.title: Filled quantity by side
panels.description: Quantity, not fill count. One fill of 10,000 and ten fills of 1,000 are operationally different, and only this panel tells them apart.

panels.title: Order round trip (in-process)
panels.description: Submit to final ExecutionReport. EXCLUDES network, kernel and venue time, which dominate a real deployment — this measures the connectivity layer's own cost, not wire-to-wire latency.

panels.title: Pre-trade risk — what was stopped, and why
Kill switch
panels.description: 1 when engaged. A state, so a gauge — a counter here would be meaningless.

panels.title: Pre-trade decisions by reason
panels.description: The reason label is what makes this actionable. 'Rejections are up' is not a finding; 'price_collar rejections are up' points at a stale reference price, and 'position_limit' points at a mandate.

panels.title: Market data quality by verdict
panels.description: A gap means messages were lost and the book needs recovery. A duplicate means the transport is retransmitting. A reorder means it is not preserving order. Three different faults that all look like 'bad sequence number'.

panels.title: P&L by component
panels.description: Realised and unrealised are separated because they are different kinds of number: realised is a fact that never moves with the market, unrealised is an opinion only as good as its mark.

panels.title: Positions with no fresh mark
panels.description: Open positions EXCLUDED from unrealised P&L because their mark is stale or missing. Any non-zero value means the P&L total on this dashboard is PARTIAL — which is why it is a panel and not a footnote.

panels.title: Working parents
panels.description: Parent orders currently being executed. A parent that stays here without its slice count advancing is stuck.

panels.title: Implementation shortfall (bps) vs arrival
panels.description: Signed so POSITIVE IS ALWAYS BAD: a buyer paying above arrival and a seller receiving below it are the same failure, so the two aggregate. Measured against the mid at the moment the parent was accepted — everything after that is a cost of the decision to trade. Measuring against the average of your own fills is circular and always flatters the algo.

panels.title: Consumer lag by topic and group
panels.description: The number an operator watches. Lag that grows monotonically means a consumer is falling behind permanently rather than absorbing a burst — the distinction is the slope, not the level.

panels.title: Publish failures and dead letters
panels.description: A non-zero publish failure rate means the event log is incomplete while trading continued. That is a deliberate trade — a bus failure must not fail a trade — but it must be visible, because the log is no longer a complete record.

panels.title: Top-of-book spread
panels.description: Per symbol, because an aggregate spread across instruments is not a number that means anything. A spread that widens sharply is a liquidity event; one that goes to zero is usually a data fault.
